note: Advanced Y12 differential calculus (11) + the first half of integral calculus — primitives, the definite integral as an area, the Fundamental Theorem and the power rule (11) = 22. ORDER: no in-wave prereq; the Y11 differentiation skills shipped in W3-8. `differentiate-combined-functions` also carries an Extension 1 dot point (`dp-s6x1y12-calculus-1`) — it is generated ONCE, here, and W4-9 must not re-queue it. NEAR-ANCHOR NOTE: there is no `Introduction to Differentiation 2_` booklet in `booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/`; that gap sits under the Y11 topic already shipped in W3-8, and every Year 12 dot point in this batch is covered by Differential Calculus 1–4 and Integral Calculus 1, so no skill here is `anchor: none`.

sections.name: differentiate-exponentials
bookletPaths: booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/Differential Calculus 1_Differentiation with exponential functions.md
hazards: One rule per skill. `differentiate-exponential` = $\frac{d}{dx}e^{x}=e^{x}$ and $\frac{d}{dx}e^{kx}=ke^{kx}$, plus sums and constant multiples. `differentiate-ax` = $\frac{d}{dx}a^{x}=a^{x}\ln a$ (and $\frac{d}{dx}a^{kx}=ka^{kx}\ln a$), including why the $\ln a$ appears. `differentiate-exponential-composite` = the chain rule form $\frac{d}{dx}e^{f(x)}=f'(x)e^{f(x)}$, and $e^{f(x)}$ inside a product or quotient.

$e^{x}$ IS THE ONLY EXPONENTIAL WHOSE DERIVATIVE IS ITSELF. Omitting $\ln a$ from $\frac{d}{dx}a^{x}$ is the compulsory named distractor for `differentiate-ax`, and at least one item must have $a=e$ so the student sees why the general rule collapses.

NEVER APPLY THE POWER RULE TO AN EXPONENTIAL: $\frac{d}{dx}2^{x}\ne x2^{x-1}$. That confusion must appear as a named distractor at least once, and no item may mix $x^{n}$ and $a^{x}$ in a way that lets the student get the right answer by the wrong rule.

THE INNER DERIVATIVE MULTIPLIES, IT DOES NOT REPLACE: $\frac{d}{dx}e^{3x^{2}}=6xe^{3x^{2}}$, and the exponent is UNCHANGED. 'Differentiated the exponent as well' ($6xe^{6x}$) is the compulsory named distractor for the composite skill.
ANSWERS MUST BE PINNED TO ONE FORM. $2e^{2x}$, $2\cdot e^{2x}$ and $\frac{2}{e^{-2x}}$ are the same number; state 'in simplest form' in every stem and never offer two algebraically equal options.
This section is figure-free: emit no [tikz] blocks. Nothing here asks for a curve to be sketched — the graphical applications belong to W4-6.

sections.name: differentiate-logarithms
bookletPaths: booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/Differential Calculus 2_Differentiation with logarithmic functions.md
hazards: One rule per skill. `differentiate-ln` = $\frac{d}{dx}\ln x=\frac{1}{x}$ (with the domain $x>0$), plus constant multiples and sums. `differentiate-loga` = $\frac{d}{dx}\log_{a}x=\frac{1}{x\ln a}$ via the change of base. `differentiate-ln-composite` = $\frac{d}{dx}\ln f(x)=\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$, including $\ln$ inside a product or quotient.

$\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)}$, NOT $\frac{1}{f(x)}$ AND NOT $\frac{1}{f'(x)}$ — both omissions must appear as named distractors on the composite skill, and at least one item must have $f'(x)$ non-constant so the difference is visible.

SIMPLIFY THE LOGARITHM BEFORE DIFFERENTIATING where the log laws allow it ($\ln(x^{3})=3\ln x$, $\ln\frac{x}{x+1}=\ln x-\ln(x+1)$). At least one item must be far easier that way, and its solution must show the simplification as its first line. Both routes must give the same simplified answer — verify that before keying.

THE DOMAIN IS PART OF THE ANSWER when the item asks for it: $\ln f(x)$ requires $f(x)>0$. Never write $\ln(x-3)$ and then evaluate a derivative at $x=2$ — that is a false premise the arithmetic audit cannot see. Check every evaluation point lies in the domain.
$\ln a$ IS A CONSTANT, so $\frac{1}{x\ln a}$ is not $\frac{\ln a}{x}$ and not $\frac{1}{x}\ln a$. Pin the form and never offer two equivalent writings of the same derivative.
This section is figure-free: emit no [tikz] blocks.

sections.name: differentiate-trigonometric
bookletPaths: booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/Differential Calculus 3_Differentiation with trigonometric functions.md
hazards: One rule per skill. `differentiate-sin-cos` = $\frac{d}{dx}\sin x=\cos x$, $\frac{d}{dx}\cos x=-\sin x$ and the $\sin kx$/$\cos kx$ forms. `differentiate-tan-reciprocal-trig` = $\frac{d}{dx}\tan x=\sec^{2}x$, $\frac{d}{dx}\sec x=\sec x\tan x$, $\frac{d}{dx}\csc x=-\csc x\cot x$, $\frac{d}{dx}\cot x=-\csc^{2}x$. `differentiate-trig-composite` = the chain rule on $\sin f(x)$ etc., and trig inside a product or quotient.

EVERYTHING IN THIS TOPIC IS IN RADIANS. State it in the theory and keep every item in radians: the derivative formulas are FALSE in degrees. No item may print a degree symbol, and any evaluation point is a multiple or fraction of $\pi$.

THE MINUS SIGN ON $\cos$, $\csc$ AND $\cot$ IS THE TOPIC'S WHOLE DIFFICULTY. Every skill needs at least one item where dropping a minus sign lands on an offered option, and 'lost the negative' must be a named distractor with the slip stated.

$\frac{d}{dx}\sin^{2}x=2\sin x\cos x$ — the chain rule applies to the POWER as well as the argument. Distinguish $\sin^{2}x$, $\sin(x^{2})$ and $\sin 2x$ explicitly; put at most one of them in any one option list, since their derivatives are easily confused but genuinely different.

$2\sin x\cos x$ AND $\sin 2x$ ARE EQUAL — never offer both as options, and pin the required form in the stem when a double-angle identity could rewrite the answer. Same for $\sec^{2}x$ versus $1+\tan^{2}x$.
This section is figure-free: emit no [tikz] blocks.

sections.name: using-derivatives
hazards: `differentiate-combined-functions` = choosing and combining the product, quotient and chain rules on functions built from exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric and polynomial pieces — the point is the CHOICE and the nesting ($x^{2}e^{3x}$, $\frac{\ln x}{\sin x}$, $e^{\sin 2x}$), not any one rule. `tangents-normals-advanced` = the equation of a tangent or normal to any of these curves at a stated point, and the reverse (where is the tangent horizontal, or parallel to a given line).

THIS SKILL ALSO CARRIES AN EXTENSION 1 DOT POINT but is generated once, here, at the Advanced level. Do not reach into Extension 1 material: no parametric differentiation, no inverse-function derivative, no inverse trigonometric functions. Those are separate skills in W4-9.

THE PRODUCT RULE IS NOT $u'v'$ AND THE QUOTIENT RULE'S NUMERATOR IS $u'v-uv'$ IN THAT ORDER. Reversing the quotient numerator is the compulsory named distractor; build at least one item where the reversed version is a plausible offered answer.

A NORMAL'S GRADIENT IS $-\frac{1}{m}$, NOT $-m$ AND NOT $\frac{1}{m}$ — and a horizontal tangent has a VERTICAL normal ($x=c$), which has no gradient at all. Include that case and state the equation correctly; 'wrote $y=c$ for the vertical normal' is a good named distractor.

EVERY TANGENT AND NORMAL ITEM THAT CARRIES A FIGURE MUST DERIVE THE LINE FROM THE PLOTTED FUNCTION — plot the curve with a `domain=`-restricted function plot, compute the gradient at the point of contact, and draw the line from that gradient. Hand-picked coordinate lists with an eyeballed tangent fail `audit-tangent-lines.mjs`. Never use `^` inside a plotted TikZ expression: write $e^{x}$ as `exp(x)` and $2^{x}$ as `exp(x*ln(2))`. Restrict every plot's domain to the axis window and compute where the curve leaves it.

The shipped Y11 skills `tangent-normal-equations` and `points-given-gradient` own tangents to polynomials. This section takes the space they cannot: every curve here involves an exponential, a logarithm or a trigonometric function.

Verify every stated point actually lies ON the curve before keying the item — substituting the $x$ value must reproduce the $y$ value exactly. A point off the curve is a false premise the gate cannot see.

sections.name: primitives
bookletPaths: booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/Integral Calculus 1_The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.md
hazards: One routine per skill. `primitive-definition` = what a primitive (antiderivative) IS — $F'(x)=f(x)$ — verifying a candidate by differentiating it, and why the family differs by a constant. `primitive-power-functions` = $\int x^{n}\,dx=\frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C$ for $n\ne-1$, including negative and fractional $n$. `primitive-linear-power` = $\int(ax+b)^{n}\,dx=\frac{(ax+b)^{n+1}}{a(n+1)}+C$. `primitive-initial-condition` = recovering the specific function from its derivative plus a point.

$+C$ IS NOT OPTIONAL on any indefinite primitive, and an option that omits it is a legitimate named distractor exactly once per skill. Conversely `primitive-initial-condition` answers carry NO $C$ — it has been evaluated.

$n=-1$ IS EXCLUDED FROM THE POWER RULE ($\frac{x^{0}}{0}$ is undefined). Say so in the theory, include one item that asks which power the rule cannot handle, and never let $\int x^{-1}dx$ appear with a power-rule answer. The logarithmic primitive belongs to W4-5.

THE $\frac{1}{a}$ IN `primitive-linear-power` IS THE COMPULSORY NAMED DISTRACTOR: $\int(3x+2)^{4}dx=\frac{(3x+2)^{5}}{15}+C$, not $\frac{(3x+2)^{5}}{5}$. At least two thirds of that skill's items must have $a\ne1$.

REWRITE BEFORE INTEGRATING: $\frac{1}{x^{3}}=x^{-3}$ and $\sqrt{x}=x^{1/2}$. At least one item per skill must require that rewriting, and its solution must show the rewritten line first. 'Integrated the denominator' is a named distractor.

EVERY PRIMITIVE MUST BE VERIFIED BY DIFFERENTIATING IT BACK before the item is keyed — that check is one line and catches every arithmetic slip in this section. Show it in at least one solution per skill.
This section is figure-free: emit no [tikz] blocks.

sections.name: definite-integral-as-area
bookletPaths: booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/Integral Calculus 1_The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.md
hazards: One routine per skill. `definite-integral-limit-sum` = the CONCEPT — $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx$ as the limit of a sum of rectangle areas as their width tends to zero, and reading the notation's parts. `approximate-area-rectangles` = actually computing a left-endpoint, right-endpoint or midpoint rectangle approximation (and a trapezium approximation) over a stated number of strips, and saying whether it over- or under-estimates. `definite-integral-geometric` = evaluating an integral by recognising the region as triangles, rectangles, trapezia or a semicircle — NO primitive is used.

OVER- vs UNDER-ESTIMATE DEPENDS ON WHETHER THE FUNCTION IS INCREASING OR DECREASING: on an increasing function, left endpoints under-estimate and right endpoints over-estimate; on a decreasing one the reverse. Every `approximate-area-rectangles` item must state which endpoints are used and at least one must be on a decreasing function, with 'assumed left always under-estimates' a named distractor.

AREA BELOW THE AXIS COUNTS AS NEGATIVE in a definite integral. `definite-integral-geometric` must include one item where part of the region is below the axis, and must distinguish 'the value of the integral' from 'the total area enclosed' in the stem — those two answers differ, and offering both without pinning which is wanted is a two-correct-answer defect.
$\int_{a}^{b}=-\int_{b}^{a}$: include one item with reversed limits, and make 'ignored the order of the limits' a named distractor.

EVERY ITEM IN ALL THREE SKILLS CARRIES A `[tikz]` FIGURE — the curve with the region shaded, and for the rectangle skill the actual rectangles drawn to the stated strip width with the correct endpoint heights. Plot the curve as a function with a `domain=` restricted to the axis window (never `^` in a plotted expression); draw each rectangle's height at the endpoint the stem names, and verify by evaluating the function at every strip boundary that the drawn heights are right. A figure whose rectangles touch the curve at the wrong endpoints contradicts its own answer.
The strip width is $h=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and $n$ strips have $n+1$ boundaries — the off-by-one on how many function values are needed is the section's other named distractor.
The Fundamental Theorem does not appear in this section: no item may evaluate an integral by finding a primitive. That is the next section's skill.

sections.name: ftc-and-power-integration
bookletPaths: booklets/Stage 6 Advanced/Integral Calculus 1_The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.md
hazards: One routine per skill. `fundamental-theorem-calculus` = the statement in both directions — $\frac{d}{dx}\int_{a}^{x}f(t)dt=f(x)$, and $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx=F(b)-F(a)$ — and what it means that differentiation and integration undo each other. `indefinite-integral-notation` = reading and writing $\int f(x)dx$, the role of $dx$, and the difference between a definite and an indefinite integral. `integrate-power-rule` = evaluating definite integrals of polynomials and power functions. `reverse-chain-rule-power` = $\int f'(x)[f(x)]^{n}dx=\frac{[f(x)]^{n+1}}{n+1}+C$, recognising when the derivative of the inner function is present as a factor.

$F(b)-F(a)$ IN THAT ORDER, and the $+C$ CANCELS in a definite integral so it must not appear in the answer. 'Computed $F(a)-F(b)$' is the compulsory named distractor for `integrate-power-rule`, and at least a third of items must produce a negative value so the sign error is visible.

THE REVERSE CHAIN RULE NEEDS THE INNER DERIVATIVE TO BE PRESENT UP TO A CONSTANT. $\int 2x(x^{2}+1)^{3}dx$ works; $\int(x^{2}+1)^{3}dx$ does NOT by this method. Include one item asking which of several integrals the method applies to, and never key an item that silently invents the missing factor.

AN INDEFINITE INTEGRAL IS A FUNCTION AND A DEFINITE INTEGRAL IS A NUMBER. Never place a function and a number in one option list, and make 'left the answer as a function when a number was asked for' a named distractor exactly once.

EVERY DEFINITE-INTEGRAL VALUE MUST BE RE-COMPUTED DIGIT BY DIGIT and checked for sign against the picture: if the region lies above the axis the answer is positive. A keyed value whose sign contradicts the region is the defect class no gate script catches.

FIGURES: `fundamental-theorem-calculus` carries one reference figure showing the accumulating area under a curve from $a$ to a moving $x$, and definite-integral items shade the region between the curve and the axis over the stated limits. Plot curves as functions restricted to the axis window; never `^` inside a plotted expression.
Exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric integrands do NOT appear in this section — they are W4-5's skills. Keep every integrand a polynomial or a power of $x$ (or of a linear expression).
